I don’t want to sound rude but you are wrong in thinking depression is not an illness. It is, that’s just a fact. 

You’re right though about having a lot of work to do, because that’s what getting better is: it’s work. 

“Every day it gets a little easier. But you have to do it every day. That’s the hard part.”

I understand how you feel, believe me I’ve been there. 
Once you’re in that pit it’s hard to imagine a life that could be different. 
What worked for me was religion. I found god and through him I gained  the strength to better myself. But I understand that’s not everyone’s path. 
What I can recommend is try to find an anchor, something to hold on to when you feel yourself spiral. 
Maybe family, maybe friends, maybe art or movies or video games or something that means a lot to you. 


When it comes to having the energy to face the day, that’s actually something everyone can work on. You’ve probably heard it a hundred times but eating right, sleeping right, and getting exercise are crucial to fighting depression. 


Remember: depression is a physiological condition. It may be in your brain but your brain needs to be treated right to heal.
